reviewBoundary: Three complete original junior fifteen-gap four-choice narratives: race drinks, an organised walking group and a kitchen sound. Fictional incidents; same-author contextual/key/all-alternative review, not independent calibration.

materials.title: The drinks after the race
materials.text:
Our class sold lemonade at a charity sports morning. We arranged a bright sign and cups. When the runners passed us without stopping, I thought the drink must look ____1____.

I wanted to add more fruit to the jug. My friend Rosa asked me to wait. The runners were in the middle of a ____2____. They could not stop for our attractive table.

The organisers already had water at the course's drinking point. Our lemonade was an extra treat to enjoy ____3____, not a replacement. We had chosen the right place but perhaps the wrong ____4____ to expect customers.

Rosa checked the schedule. The first group would finish in twenty minutes. We moved the sign so it could be seen from the finish area and kept the cups ____5____ until people arrived.

Soon families began walking over. Some wanted lemonade, while others asked where the toilets were. We answered those questions too. A stall did not become useful only when someone made a ____6____.

By noon, most of the lemonade was gone. I was glad we had not changed the recipe in a ____7____. Nobody had tried it when I first worried.

After cleaning the table, we counted the money and gave it to the organiser. Rosa wrote down the busiest ____8____ for next year's class. I noted the sign’s position.

I had been judging success by the first few ____9____. Waiting had given us a fairer picture. That did not mean every quiet stall should simply wait ____10____. It meant asking what the people nearby were actually doing before guessing what they ____11____. Preparation mattered, but so did their ____12____. Next time, I would read the event plan before decorating the cups. A good idea needed more than a colourful ____13____. It needed to meet people at a useful ____14____ in their day. Rosa called it common sense. I was glad to have ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator fears the drink fails to attract, hence uninviting. Delicious/familiar are not negative appearance judgments; price is not the proposed extra-fruit solution.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Runners are racing and cannot stop to buy. A queue/shop/break would not be the stated running task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Afterwards means after the race, when runners can stop for a treat. Beforehand/previously refer to before this point and immediately contradicts their current inability to stop.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The key issue is when customers can stop. Recipe/colour/name are not the schedule problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Covered cups stay protected until service. Empty would be a drink state rather than preparation, hidden prevents service and broken unusable.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Answering directions helps even without a purchase. Mistake/speech/journey do not name buying from the stall.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The narrator wanted an anxious rushed change, a panic. Kitchen/book/race do not name that reaction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Noting busy times helps future scheduling. Recipes/families/prices do not address when demand appeared.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The first few minutes were an unfairly short assessment period. Cups/lemons/tables are objects rather than elapsed observation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The qualified lesson rejects waiting forever as a universal answer. Indoor/outdoor location and solitude are not the limit on endless waiting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Activities help infer what people want, rather than assume rejection. Carried/paid/wore do not name the need being misread.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The runners’ schedule determines when a treat fits. Money/names/clothes are not the race-timing constraint.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: A colourful sign represents attractive promotion beyond which timing matters. Jug/table/fruit are not described as colourful display text.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: A useful moment in the day expresses timing. Price/distance/number do not fit that temporal opportunity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The narrator has learned common sense through the event. Selling/forgetting/drawing do not acquire the lesson.

materials.title: A bus with no wheels
materials.text:
A school sign announced a "walking bus". Finn brought his bus card. He expected a vehicle. Instead, he found a teacher and several children wearing bright ____1____.

The teacher explained: approved adults led a group walking to school. It followed an agreed route and picked up children at set ____2____. Parents arranged participation beforehand.

Finn laughed at his mistake and put his card ____3____. He joined the group for the short walk. One adult stayed at the front and another at the ____4____, keeping everyone together.

At the first corner, the group stopped even though Finn wanted to keep going. A younger child needed time to ____5____ a shoelace. The others waited safely.

They arrived at school with time to spare. Finn had expected walking together to be ____6____ than taking a real bus. It was surprisingly straightforward.

After a week, he knew the children who joined at different stops. The route remained the same, but the ____7____ changed each day. Sometimes they talked about lessons; sometimes they noticed a bird on a wall.

 It was not a literal ____8____, but it explained a useful arrangement. A route, regular times and responsible leaders made the walk something families could ____9____.

Finn did not decide that every journey should be made on foot. Distance, weather and people's needs could make other choices ____10____. He had simply found another way to make his own morning ____11____. His card stayed ready for longer trips. The bright jacket helped others see him, but it did not ____12____ the need to follow instructions. A clever name was a beginning, not the whole ____13____. When asked, Finn explained the name. He remembered how a familiar word had ____14____ him, and how a simple question had put him back on the right ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Bright jackets make the group visible, explicitly recalled near the end. The other clothing/items are not identified as the group’s marked outfit.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A route picks children up at set stops. Prices/tables/lessons do not name collection points.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Finn puts his unneeded card away. Forward/outside/upstairs do not mean storing it for later.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Adults cover front and back of the group. Shop/school/corner are locations, not the opposite position to front.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: A child needs to tie a shoelace. Cutting/buying/finding do not express securing the undone lace.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Finn expects walking to take longer, slower than a vehicle. Shorter concerns route length, cost/noise are not the arriving-with-time contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Talk varies each day despite an unchanged route. The route itself remains the same, and school/weather are not the topics’ shifting exchange.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The walking bus is not literally a vehicle. Jackets/leaders/signs are physically present.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Agreed times and approved leaders make a dependable arrangement to trust. Avoiding rejects it; carrying/selling do not name reliability.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Other transport choices may suit different distances, weather and needs. Impossible denies alternatives, identical ignores difference and invisible is irrelevant.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The arrangement makes Finn’s particular short journey easier. Longer/later/stranger are not the positive practical improvement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A visible jacket does not remove the duty to follow instructions. Create implies no prior duty, explain is information and increase a larger burden, not the erased-obligation assumption being rejected.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: A name alone is not the whole operational plan. Price/word/road do not include leaders, timing and rules.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Bus initially misled Finn into expecting a vehicle. Frightened is unsupported; helped/welcomed do not express his mistaken interpretation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: On the right track means correctly understanding again. Bus/card/jacket are literal items, not the idiomatic corrected direction.

materials.title: The noise beside the fridge
materials.text:
A strange buzzing began in our kitchen one evening. Dad looked towards the fridge and frowned. It was old, and he thought the sound meant an expensive ____1____. He searched for repair services.

My sister asked when the buzzing had started. We were unsure. It seemed louder when a lorry passed outside, but that connection might have been a ____2____. We listened again.

We did not open the machine or touch its workings. Instead, we checked the objects ____3____ it. A metal tray leaned against the counter, and a spoon rested across its edge. When my sister moved the spoon, the sound ____4____.

The fridge had been running normally. A small vibration had made the loose objects ____5____ against one another. The noise sounded expensive only because we had already ____6____ it to the oldest appliance in the room.

Dad put down his phone and laughed. He did not conclude that every unusual sound was ____7____. A real fault would still need proper attention. This one simply had another explanation.

My sister's question had been more useful than my confident statement that the fridge was ____8____. She had separated what we heard from what we ____9____ about its cause.

I considered my other quick conclusions. A friend who replied late was not necessarily angry; a difficult homework question was not necessarily impossible. Different situations, yet the same ____10____ could appear: a small observation growing into a complete story too quickly.

Checking did not mean rejecting the first idea just to be ____11____. It meant looking for something that could support or ____12____ it. One spoon had done that. The answer was simple, but finding it required a little ____13____. We kept the number; appliances do break. We also moved the tray to a better ____14____. The evening ended with a quieter kitchen and one less ____15____ on Dad's list.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Dad anticipates an expensive repair and searches services. Decoration, travel and food are not the suspected machine cost.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The lorry’s timing may be coincidence, not causation. Promise/rule/record do not name an accidental connection.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The title and counter tray locate the source beside the fridge. Inside is explicitly not opened, while above/behind are not the stated counter relation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Moving the spoon removes the buzz, so stopped. Growth/return/spread contradict the solved source.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Vibration makes loose metal objects rattle. Sleep/melting/shining do not create that sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: They attribute the noise to the fridge before checking. Selling/carrying/returning do not name assigning a cause.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The family does not generalise one harmless noise to all sounds. Expensive was the mistaken worry; familiar/permanent do not define danger versus safe.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The narrator initially asserts the fridge is broken. Empty/new/quiet do not describe the assumed fault.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: She separates the observed sound from assumptions about its cause. Recorded/noticed/heard are observation activities, not the inferred explanation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The common pattern is an observation becoming an overconfident story. Noise/spoon/appliance belong only to the kitchen, not the other social/homework examples.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: They need not reject an idea merely to be different. Certainty/quickness/safety do not express pointless disagreement for its own sake.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Evidence can support or challenge an idea. Repetition/printing/hiding do not test whether the explanation fits.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Listening and checking require patience. Money, extra noise and glue do not help establish this cause.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The tray is moved to a better position to prevent vibration contact. Price/time/colour are not its physical placement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Dad has one less worry about costly repair. The spoon and repair number are retained, and food is not the concern.
